claims.statement: The proxy delegates upstream authentication and request mutation to Provider::prepare_request before sending the request; AnthropicOAuthProvider uses that seam to mutate both headers and parsed JSON and return the selected account ID for upstream error handling.
The presence of [oauth] selects OAuth pool mode and suppresses [[headers]] configuration; the committed Kubernetes configuration uses OAuth mode.

Passthrough applies valid configured static headers without selecting an account or parsing or changing the body; it refuses to inject or overwrite Authorization, and a configured anthropic-beta replaces rather than merges with the client value.

Before provider preparation the handler filters hop-by-hop headers, Host, and Content-Length so that the outbound client uses the upstream host and frames the reserialized OAuth body without the inbound byte count.
Invalid JSON in OAuth mode produces HTTP 400 before account selection; provider preparation failures including pool exhaustion produce HTTP 503 rather than sending the request.
The pool selects usable accounts by round-robin scan and can refresh a near-expiry credential inline before giving it to the provider.

A quota-classified upstream failure puts the selected account into cooldown and triggers failover when another attempt is available; failover preparation starts from clean copies of the filtered headers and parsed JSON, while transport timeout retries within an attempt reuse the prepared headers and body.
OAuth mode removes the client Authorization and x-api-key and sets Authorization to the selected account's OAuth Bearer credential, so clients should not send real Anthropic API keys to this gateway.

OAuth beta merging writes a single comma-separated value with the ten required flags first, then distinct nonempty client flags in order after trimming; it reads one HeaderMap value rather than aggregating repeated fields or combining body flags.

The forced beta list reflects the Claude Code 2.1.198 capture rather than the full 2.1.280 capture; adding a forced beta affects all OAuth clients and can alter response shape even when upstream accepts it.

The OAuth provider overwrites user-agent with claude-cli/2.1.280 (external, sdk-cli), x-app with cli, anthropic-version with 2023-06-01, and anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access with true, using source literals rather than client settings.
In OAuth mode x-anthropic-billing-header is stripped if present and never injected; the provider also does not synthesize the attribution system block seen in genuine Claude Code.

Claude Code debug attribution text was historically copied into a proxy header but was not proof of an HTTP header on genuine traffic; the 2.1.280 capture located genuine attribution in a system block instead.
In the INC-2026-001 live Fable comparison, clearing claude_code_version_too_old required changing the User-Agent version, not changing the retired billing attribution version.
The live D003 attribution A/B returned 200 with and without the legacy billing header, supporting retirement for acceptance; those responses did not establish which plan paid for the requests.

OAuth system prefix injection uses the shared REQUIRED_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX when model is a string, including Haiku; it skips a missing or non-string model and leaves unsupported system types unchanged.

For prefix injection, a missing system field becomes a single text-block array and a string is converted to an array with a separate prefix block only if needed; for array input all existing blocks and metadata are kept and any text block already starting with the prefix prevents insertion.

After prefix injection the Pi sanitizer only visits a system string or the text of system text blocks; it removes a recognized tagged Pi docs element while keeping surrounding sections, or removes the legacy paragraph tail while retaining date and working-directory lines, and leaves unmatched text alone.

A Pi-only extra-usage 400 can reflect an unmatched client prompt layout rather than identity header drift, as observed with the Pi 0.87.1 update; a successful minimal client test does not cover that prompt shape.
The OAuth provider's JSON mutations are limited to system, preserving other parsed fields such as model, messages, tools, parameters, and stream even though the proxy reserializes the JSON.
Forgeflare's historical tool-name compatibility fix was client-side, while the proposed OpenClaw tool rewrite profile remains a deferred draft, not an implemented OAuth request transformation.

The D002 synthetic regression calls the actual OAuth preparation seam twice using fresh temporary stores and inert non-expiring credentials, requiring consistent observations; it does not send the messages request upstream and does not establish live acceptance, SSE parity, or plan usage.

D002 checks exact User-Agent and fixed headers, removal and replacement of client credentials, absence of the retired billing header, required-first beta union with overlap de-duplication, and equality of the fixture body except for expected system injection; observations include only allowlisted public headers and protection checks rather than credentials or request content.

Pi sanitizer cases are covered separately from the no-system D002 fixture, and service tests with a local upstream echo server check billing-header stripping and beta merging after forwarding through the handler.
